papers.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery.
papers.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 00
papers.summary: DBAASP v4 is a manually curated database that links peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative bioactivity measurements (antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, cytotoxicity) along with the experimental conditions under which they were obtained. The update adds chemical structure information and condition-resolved labels, providing context-rich data needed to train machine learning models for peptide and peptidomimetic discovery.

papers.title: PROTAC-DB 4.0: an expanded knowledgebase of targeted protein degradation modalities with AI-powered knowledge discovery.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent an emerging therapeutic modality that harnesses the ubiquitin-proteasome system to induce targeted protein degradation (TPD). Their event-driven and catalytic mechanisms provide new opportunities to target previously undruggable proteins. However, the rapid expansion of TPD technologies, including molecular glues (MGs) and X-functional targeting chimeras (XTACs), together with the increasing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in degrader design, highlights the need for comprehensive and continuously updated data resources. Here, we pr
papers.summary: PROTAC-DB 4.0 is an updated knowledgebase that expands beyond classical PROTACs to include other targeted protein degradation modalities such as molecular glues and XTACs. It also incorporates AI-powered knowledge discovery tools to help researchers navigate and mine the growing body of degrader data, supporting the design of new therapeutic degraders.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Enzyme Classification via Multiple Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate Enzyme Commission (EC) number prediction is fundamental to protein function annotation and metabolic pathway reconstruction. Recent methods based on protein language model embeddings or 3D structure have improved EC prediction, but important limitations remain. Whole-sequence embeddings can dilute local functional signals, such as catalytic residues and functional domains, whereas structure-based methods depend on accurate protein structures and are therefore difficult to apply broadly.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a domain-aware enzyme classification method that uses multiple instance learning to focus on local functional regions (like catalytic residues and domains) rather than whole-sequence embeddings, avoiding reliance on accurate 3D structures. This addresses limitations of existing protein language model and structure-based EC number prediction approaches.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure.
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files ra
papers.summary: dictyBase, the model organism database for Dictyostelium discoideum, has been completely reimplemented as a self-contained service built on static data files and minimal infrastructure. This redesign preserves two decades of genomic data, protocols, stock center information, and community resources while reducing maintenance burden. The new architecture offers a sustainable model for small community databases facing resource constraints.

papers.title: Assessment of LLMs on basic bioinformatics tasks requiring multi-step reasoning and code writing.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), AI agents and co-scientists promise to accelerate scientific discovery across fields ranging from chemistry to biology. Bioinformatics- the analysis of DNA, RNA and protein sequences plays a crucial role in biological research and is especially amenable to AI-driven automation given its computational nature. Here, we assess the bioinformatics capabilities of popular general-purpose LLMs on a set of tasks covering basic analytical questions that include code writing and multi-step reasoning in the domain.
papers.summary: This study evaluates how well popular general-purpose large language models handle basic bioinformatics tasks that require both writing code and multi-step reasoning. The authors find that while LLMs show promise for automating computational biology workflows, their performance varies across tasks, highlighting current limitations and areas for improvement.

papers.title: Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming embedded in microbiome research, yet the way microbiome scientists are trained has not kept pace. Existing discussions frequently emphasize AI literacy and responsible tool use. We argue that literacy alone is insufficient in a field where data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, inappropriate model selection and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. We propose an AI-competence framework comprising five connected capabilities: data and platform fluency, machine-learning comp
papers.summary: The authors argue that microbiome researchers need deeper AI competence rather than basic AI literacy, because common pitfalls like data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. They propose a five-part AI-competence framework covering data and platform fluency, machine-learning competency, and related skills to guide training in the field.

papers.title: pdb2reaction: End-to-End Reaction-Path Elucidation from PDB Structures Using Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials.
papers.abstract: Elucidating enzymatic reaction mechanisms requires a sequence of computational tasks comprising active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state (TS) refinement, intrinsic reaction coordinate (IRC) validation, and quasi-rigid-rotor harmonic-oscillator (QRRHO) thermochemistrystages typically connected by ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning. We present pdb2reaction, an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates this entire pipeline directly from a user-curated PDB using a single machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) backend. A GPU-accelerated pysisyphu
papers.summary: pdb2reaction is an open-source Python command-line toolkit that automates the full enzymatic reaction-mechanism workflow—active-site extraction, minimum-energy-path search, transition-state refinement, IRC validation, and QRRHO thermochemistry—starting directly from a user-curated PDB file. It uses a single machine-learning interatomic potential backend with GPU acceleration, replacing the ad hoc scripting and per-system tuning typically required to connect these stages.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Protein Secondary-Structure Segmentation in Intermediate-Resolution Cryo-EM Maps: A Resolution-Stratified Benchmark Dataset and Controlled Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of protein secondary structures in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps is crucial for protein tracing and atomic model building, yet remains challenging at intermediate resolutions. Although deep learning architectures have recently been applied to this task, there remains a lack of standardized evaluation protocols and systematic resolution-stratified analyses. Consequently, it remains unclear how segmentation performance varies across finer resolution ranges within the intermediate-resolution regime and how different volumetric segmentation architectures compare und
papers.summary: This paper introduces a resolution-stratified benchmark dataset and a controlled evaluation protocol for deep-learning-based segmentation of protein secondary structures in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. It systematically compares volumetric segmentation architectures across finer resolution ranges, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation in this regime. The work aims to clarify how segmentation performance degrades with resolution and which architectures perform best.

papers.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
papers.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. OmniVira implements an auditable article-evidence framework linking individual findings and supporting text to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities, and relevan
papers.summary: OmniVira is a curated knowledgebase that consolidates literature-derived evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission into structured, source-linked records. Each finding is tied to normalized virus, host, and geographic entities with traceable supporting text, enabling reusable and auditable evidence for zoonotic emergence research.

papers.title: A compact generative language model learns the compositional grammar of phase-separating proteins.
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of intrinsically disordered proteins drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, yet the sequence-level grammar that promotes condensation remains difficult to specify from first principles. Existing protein language models are typically trained on large, folded-protein-rich sequence corpora and may not optimally capture the compositional biases of LLPS-prone disordered proteins. Here, we show that a compact generative language model, with an architecture and size (∼17 M parameters) selected via systematic hyperparameter optimization and cross-valida
papers.summary: The authors trained a compact generative language model (~17M parameters) specifically on phase-separating intrinsically disordered proteins, showing that a small, well-optimized model can capture the compositional sequence grammar driving liquid-liquid phase separation. This suggests that domain-specific small models can outperform large general-purpose protein language models for disordered protein tasks.

papers.title: Prediction of Residue-Level Base Preference for DNA-Binding Proteins Using a Multimodal Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: Specific recognition between proteins and DNA governs essential cellular functions, yet the binding specificity of most DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) remains experimentally uncharacterized and high-throughput experimental methods still lag far behind the ever-growing protein data set. Here, we present 3M-BSIP (3-modal base-specific interaction predictor), a multimodal deep learning framework capable of predicting the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DBPs. 3M-BSIP constructs a holistic protein representation by integrating three distinct modalities: a protein language m
papers.summary: The authors present 3M-BSIP, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the DNA-binding interface and residue-level base preference for DNA-binding proteins. It integrates three protein representation modalities, including a protein language model, to address the gap between the growing number of known proteins and the limited experimental characterization of their DNA-binding specificity. This offers a computational route to annotate binding specificity for the many DBPs lacking experimental data.

papers.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning.
papers.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion
papers.summary: The authors present AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework that uses a large language model to guide parallel multi-site sequence editing for optimizing therapeutic antibodies across multiple properties simultaneously. The method identifies promising edit sites and actions (substitution, insertion, deletion, or reservation) to navigate the vast sequence space despite sparse annotations and property tradeoffs. This addresses a key bottleneck in antibody drug development where experimentally identified candidates require further optimization.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other
papers.summary: This study compared 7T fMRI brain responses from 30 participants reading 108 carefully designed sentences against representations from eight transformer-based large language models and eleven other models. The sentences were constructed to separate sentence structure from word meaning, and representational similarity analysis showed that transformer models poorly capture how word order shapes neural representations of sentence meaning. The findings suggest that despite producing human-like language, LLMs do not encode meaning in a human-like way.

papers.title: Protein-Protein Interface Residue Prediction by Integrating Protein Language Representations and Structural Graph Attention.
papers.abstract: Accurate residue-level prediction of protein-protein interaction interfaces is important for elucidating molecular recognition mechanisms and guiding targeted drug design. However, interface residues are relatively sparse and governed by complex spatial dependencies, making their accurate identification challenging. In this study, we developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model based on the PDBbind v2020.R1 data set. To reduce information leakage arising from sequence homology, receptor and ligand sequences were clustered independently, and the resulting clusters were used to co
papers.summary: The authors developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model that combines protein language model representations with structural graph attention to predict which residues lie at protein-protein interfaces. They built it on PDBbind v2020.R1 with homology-aware clustering to reduce information leakage between training and test sets. The approach targets the sparse, spatially complex nature of interface residues to improve residue-level prediction for drug design applications.

papers.title: Transformer Models in Vibrational Spectroscopy: A Review.
papers.abstract: Transformer models have attracted increasing interest in vibrational spectroscopy because of their ability to capture long-range dependencies in spectral data. These models have been applied to analytical tasks including spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal data fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. Their flexible architectures support applications in Raman, infrared (IR), near-infrared (NIR), and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), with examples across chemistry, biology, and materials science. Transformer-based models also offer opportuniti
papers.summary: This review surveys the growing use of Transformer models in vibrational spectroscopy (Raman, IR, NIR, SERS) for tasks such as spectral preprocessing, classification, quantitative analysis, multimodal fusion, and spectra-to-structure prediction. It highlights how Transformer architectures capture long-range dependencies in spectral data and support applications across chemistry, biology, and materials science.

papers.title: AIDCare: A Technical Proof-of-Concept for Integrating Personalized Nutrition, Physical Activity, and AI-Assisted Care in Diabetes Lifestyle Management.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical nutrition therapy and structured lifestyle self-management are fundamental to diabetes care, yet conventional mobile health tools typically track diet, physical activity, and glucose measurements in isolation, with limited connection to clinical oversight. This study presents AIDCare, an integrated mobile health platform that connects camera-based nutritional assessment, wearable physical activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and clinician-supervised conversational artificial intelligence (AI) to support personalized dietary and lifestyle self-management i
papers.summary: AIDCare is a proof-of-concept mobile health platform that combines camera-based food recognition, wearable activity tracking, physiological monitoring, and a clinician-supervised conversational AI to support personalized diabetes lifestyle management. The work demonstrates technical integration of these components rather than reporting clinical outcomes, positioning it as an early-stage tool for connecting self-management data with clinical oversight.

papers.title: Use of Demineralized Autologous Dentin Graft with the Tooth Processing Device in Immediate Post-Extraction Implant Placement and Loading: A 12-Month Evaluation of Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Stability.
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of immediate implant placement and loading combined with autologous dentin grafting in reducing post-extraction tissue remodelling, with particular emphasis on peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone. Materials and Methods: This retrospective observational study included 13 patients (14 implant sites) with Type 1 extraction sockets in the anterior maxilla. Following atraumatic tooth extraction, implants were immediately placed and grafted with autologous dentin processed from the extracted tooth using the Tooth Transformer device. Screw-re
papers.summary: This retrospective study evaluated 13 patients (14 implant sites) who received immediate dental implants with autologous dentin grafts processed from their extracted teeth using a dedicated device. Over 12 months, the approach appeared to support peri-implant soft tissue stability in the esthetic zone, suggesting autologous dentin may help reduce post-extraction tissue remodeling. The small sample and observational design limit the strength of the conclusions.

papers.title: FusionEP: Adaptive Cross-Modal Deep Fusion Network for Essential Protein Identification via Multi-Omics Integration and Contrastive Learning.
papers.abstract: Identifying essential proteins lays a foundation for dissecting disease mechanisms and mining therapeutic targets. Existing algorithms mostly adopt unimodal inputs and struggle to capture multi-level biological interactions from genomics, subcellular localization and proteomics. We present FusionEP, which is an adaptive cross-modal deep fusion network built upon contrastive learning to predict essential proteins. FusionEP integrates gene expression profiles, subcellular localization features, and protein interaction map structures. For gene expression information, we design a six-layer Transfo
papers.summary: FusionEP is a deep learning model that predicts essential proteins by combining gene expression, subcellular localization, and protein interaction data through an adaptive cross-modal fusion network with contrastive learning. It outperforms existing unimodal approaches by capturing multi-level biological interactions across omics layers. The work demonstrates that integrating heterogeneous biological data improves essential protein identification.

papers.title: From Prediction to Generation: Artificial Intelligence Reconstructing the Paradigm of Protein Glycosylation Research.
papers.abstract: Among post-translational modifications, protein glycosylation is distinguished by its abundance and structural intricacy. Unlike protein biosynthesis, glycan assembly follows no template; it reflects glycosyltransferase/glycosidase competition, sugar-donor availability, and organelle-enforced compartmentalization, yielding heterogeneous glycoforms that confer functional versatility but complicate analysis. Three bottlenecks persist: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. Ado
papers.summary: This review argues that artificial intelligence is shifting protein glycosylation research from prediction to generation, addressing three persistent bottlenecks: stereochemical control in chemical glycosylation, ambiguous assignment of glycosylation occupancy sites, and reproducing native conformations of fully glycosylated proteins. It surveys how AI methods can model the template-free, competition-driven nature of glycan assembly and help reconstruct the field's research paradigm.

papers.title: Relation-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Learning for miRNA-Drug Response Association Prediction Under Cold-Start Generalization.
papers.abstract: (1) Background: Cancer drug resistance can be influenced by microRNAs (miRNAs), which can alter gene expression and cellular pathways that determine how cancer cells respond to treatment. Potential miRNA-drug response associations can be identified using computational models; however, evaluating these models using edge-based evaluation can result in an optimistic view of model generalization since test miRNAs or drugs can appear in other response associations during training. (2) Methods: This paper presents a relation-aware heterogeneous learning framework that integrates miRNA expression pro
papers.summary: The paper introduces a relation-aware heterogeneous graph learning framework for predicting associations between miRNAs and drug responses, with a focus on cold-start generalization where test miRNAs or drugs are unseen during training. It argues that conventional edge-based evaluation overestimates model performance and proposes a more rigorous evaluation setting. The method integrates miRNA expression profiles into a heterogeneous graph to improve prediction under these harder conditions.

papers.title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants.
papers.abstract: Over 90% of disease-associated variants from genome-wide association studies fall in noncoding regulatory regions, yet their functional interpretation remains a central open problem in genomic medicine. Large language models prompted to interpret such variants routinely hallucinate transcription factor (TF) binding changes, fabricate experimental support, and assign biological significance to statistically negligible signals. We present ARGUS (Agentic Regulatory Genomics for an Uncertainty-aware Scientist), which strictly separates deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoni
papers.summary: ARGUS is an agentic framework that interprets noncoding single nucleotide variants by strictly separating deterministic biological computation from LLM-mediated reasoning, aiming to curb hallucinations in regulatory genomics. It addresses the problem that over 90% of GWAS variants lie in noncoding regions and that LLMs often fabricate TF binding changes and experimental support. The approach constrains LLM reasoning with evidence, improving reliability of variant interpretation.

papers.title: TriTower-m6Am: A triple-tower heterogeneous deep learning architecture integrating semantic, sequential, and structural information for mRNA N6,2'-O-dimethyladenosine site prediction.
papers.abstract: N6,2'-O-dimethyladenosine (m6Am) is a cap-proximal mRNA modification deposited by PCIF1 (phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD)-interacting factor 1) at the first transcribed nucleotide of eukaryotic mRNAs. Knowing where m6Am sites sit would help explain how cells tune mRNA stability and translation, but current predictors typically depend on a single representation and do not jointly model multiple views of the same RNA sequence.
papers.summary: The authors present TriTower-m6Am, a deep learning model that combines three complementary representations of RNA sequences—semantic, sequential, and structural—to predict m6Am modification sites on mRNAs. This multi-view architecture aims to improve on existing predictors that rely on only one type of sequence representation. The work is a methodological contribution to epitranscriptomic site prediction rather than a new biological finding.

papers.title: Influence of dominant sequence artifacts on generative AI for virtual contrast-enhancement in breast MRI.
papers.abstract: Virtual contrast-enhanced (vCE) breast MRI is a deep learning approach for generating contrast-like images from non-contrast acquisitions. As diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) has emerged as a major contributor to enhancement synthesis, understanding the influence of DWI-related image artifacts is important for the robustness and potential clinical implementation of AI-based contrast-free imaging approaches. We evaluated the robustness of a pix2pix-based vCE synthesis model to artifact-contaminated DWI during training and inference.
papers.summary: This study evaluates how artifacts in diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) affect a pix2pix deep learning model that generates virtual contrast-enhanced breast MRI from non-contrast scans. The authors test model robustness when artifact-contaminated DWI data are used during both training and inference, finding that such artifacts can degrade synthesis quality. The work highlights the need for artifact-aware preprocessing before clinical deployment of AI-based contrast-free imaging.

papers.title: EvoSeq-ML: Advancing Data-Centric Machine Learning with Evolutionary-Informed Protein Sequence Representation and Generation.
papers.abstract: From protein structure prediction to novel protein generation, challenging protein engineering tasks have been made possible by advancements in machine learning (ML). While largely driven by ML architecture refinements, these advancements in ML-based protein engineering campaigns have left the impact of data curation underexplored. In light of the growing wealth of labeled sequence data, data-centric advances (e.g. prioritizing improvements in ML protein engineering tools through the curation of high-quality, domain-specific training data) are increasingly preferred over model-centric advancem
papers.summary: EvoSeq-ML argues that data curation, not just model architecture, is key to improving machine learning for protein engineering. The work introduces an evolutionary-informed approach to representing and generating protein sequences, emphasizing high-quality, domain-specific training data. It positions data-centric strategies as a preferred alternative to purely model-centric refinements.

papers.title: iTB-DRS: a multi-stage feature selection framework to identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug-resistance using single-nucleotide polymorphisms.
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance is crucial for effective tuberculosis control. However, data from genome-wide association studies are often characterized by high dimensionality and many redundant features, posing significant challenges to prediction models. To address these challenges, we propose a novel computational framework called iTB-DRS, which employs a hierarchical multi-stage feature selection strategy. The workflow begins with data encoding followed by a four-step selection mechanism, including (i) filtering noise using a Mean Decrease Accur
papers.summary: The paper introduces iTB-DRS, a computational framework that uses a hierarchical multi-stage feature selection strategy to predict Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance from single-nucleotide polymorphisms. By filtering noise and reducing redundant features from high-dimensional genome-wide association data, the approach aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of resistance prediction models.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, achieving extensive coverage of UniProtKB, and includes mappings to major resources such as Gene Ontology and PDBe. This makes it a central hub for functional annotation of protein sequences.

papers.title: Identification of plasma biomarkers for chronic kidney disease by integrating proteomics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, and early identification of individuals at risk remains challenging. This study aimed to identify plasma proteomic biomarkers associated with incident CKD and develop a machine learning-based prediction model integrating proteomic and clinical data.
papers.summary: This study integrates plasma proteomics with machine learning to identify protein biomarkers associated with incident chronic kidney disease and to build a prediction model combining proteomic and clinical data. The work aims to improve early identification of individuals at risk for CKD, addressing a major global health burden where early detection remains challenging.

papers.title: HiCP2GAN: a plug and play foundation model-based GAN for Hi-C enhancement.
papers.abstract: The 3D organization of chromatin shapes gene regulation and cellular function, and Hi-C has become the primary technique for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, high-resolution data remain costly and scarce, leaving many studies with sparse contact maps that limit downstream analysis. Deep learning methods, especially generative adversarial networks (GANs), have shown promise for enhancing low-resolution Hi-C data, but most existing GAN-based approaches rely on custom discriminators trained from scratch, which can yield unstable training and limited generalization. Hi-C founda
papers.summary: HiCP2GAN is a plug-and-play framework that uses a pretrained Hi-C foundation model as the discriminator in a GAN, rather than training a custom discriminator from scratch, to enhance low-resolution Hi-C contact maps. This leverages the foundation model's learned chromatin-interaction priors to stabilize training and improve generalization compared with conventional GAN-based Hi-C enhancement. The approach aims to make high-resolution chromatin contact maps more accessible for studies limited to sparse data.

papers.title: AxialTAD: an axial contrast architecture for TAD boundary prediction from Hi-C.
papers.abstract: Topologically associating domains (TADs) are fundamental units of 3D chromatin organization, and accurate identification of TAD boundaries from Hi-C contact matrices remains an active challenge. Recent deep learning approaches have advanced substantially, but these rely on increasingly large architectures, raising the question of how much of this capacity boundary-centric analysis requires. Here we propose AxialTAD, a compact deep learning model centered on an Axial Contrast Module (ACM) that explicitly encodes directional contrast in contact intensity along the row and column axes of local Hi
papers.summary: AxialTAD is a compact deep learning model for predicting TAD boundaries directly from Hi-C contact matrices. Its key innovation is an Axial Contrast Module that explicitly captures directional contrast in contact intensity along row and column axes, achieving strong boundary prediction without the large architectures used by prior methods. The work suggests that boundary-centric analysis may not require the massive model capacity that recent deep learning approaches have assumed.

papers.title: tModBase v2.0: an expanded database of tRNA modifications with an AI-powered assistant.
papers.abstract: Chemical modifications of transfer RNAs (tRNAs) are crucial for tRNA stability, codon decoding, translational fidelity, and tRNA-derived small RNA (tsRNA) biogenesis. Changes in these modifications are associated with stress responses, physiological regulation, and human disease, underscoring the need to integrate modification information with experimental evidence and biological context. We previously established tModBase, a web resource to organize and explore tRNA modification-related data. Its first release integrated modification sites, high-throughput sequencing-derived signals, and cond
papers.summary: tModBase v2.0 is an expanded database that integrates tRNA modification sites, high-throughput sequencing signals, and experimental evidence with biological context. The update adds an AI-powered assistant to help users explore how tRNA modifications relate to stress responses, physiology, and disease. It serves as a centralized resource for researchers studying tRNA modification biology.

papers.title: BioHarness: substrate-aware evidence assembly for biomedical question answering across literature, knowledge bases, and biological atlases.
papers.abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires evidence beyond topically retrieved literature, including gene alias resolution, database identifier normalization, and atlas-derived biological measurements. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems typically follow a fixed workflow and lack an explicit mechanism for deciding when retrieved text is sufficient, when biomedical entity mapping is needed, or when executable evidence assembly over structured measurements should be invoked. This motivates a substrate-aware large language model (LLM) harness that selectively assemble
papers.summary: BioHarness is a large language model framework that decides, per question, whether retrieved literature is enough or whether it must also resolve gene aliases, normalize database identifiers, or query biological atlases for measurements. This 'substrate-aware' routing lets it assemble evidence from text, knowledge bases, and structured data rather than relying on a fixed retrieval pipeline. The work targets biomedical question answering where topical retrieval alone is insufficient.

papers.title: Protein-based resistance in-silico model (PRISM-TB) for rapid prediction of drug-resistant tuberculosis using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Tuberculosis (TB) caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), remains a priority health challenge with multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains threatening control efforts. Conventional diagnostic methods are limited by high cost, prolonged diagnostic time and incomplete mutation coverage. This study presents PRISM-TB (Protein-based resistance in-silico model for TB), a machine learning-based framework for predicting resistance to first- and second-line anti-TB drugs using protein sequence-derived features. Methods Protein sequences of 11 resistance-associated Mycobacterium
papers.journal: The Indian journal of medical research
papers.summary: PRISM-TB is a machine learning framework that predicts resistance to first- and second-line anti-tuberculosis drugs by using features derived from protein sequences of resistance-associated Mycobacterium tuberculosis genes. It aims to overcome the cost, turnaround time, and incomplete mutation coverage of conventional drug-susceptibility testing. The abstract is truncated, so performance metrics and validation results are not available.

papers.title: The Broad Ecological Range of Salmonella enterica Serotype Typhimurium Is Associated With Genomic Diversification.
papers.abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium is a versatile foodborne pathogen with a broad ecological range, making it an ideal model to better understand pathogen adaptations that allow them to infect multiple hosts and persist across environments. Here, we analysed 595 genomes of S. Typhimurium representing three food animal sources (bovine, swine, and poultry) and one non-food animal source (wild birds). We found that S. Typhimurium from food animal sources generally had a more open pangenome and harboured more antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Notably, swine isolates exhibited the most open pangenome and
papers.summary: This study analyzed 595 genomes of Salmonella Typhimurium from bovine, swine, poultry, and wild bird sources to understand how genomic diversification enables its broad ecological range. Food animal isolates had more open pangenomes and more antimicrobial resistance genes than wild bird isolates, with swine isolates showing the most open pangenome. These findings link genomic plasticity and resistance gene acquisition to host adaptation and environmental persistence.

papers.title: Deciphering Host Genomic Pathway Landscapes in Severe COVID-19 by Exome Sequencing of a Large Admixed Brazilian Cohort.
papers.abstract: The host genetic factors that resulted in the heterogeneous clinical outcomes of COVID-19 remained poorly understood, especially in admixed populations that are underrepresented in global genomic studies. In this study, we investigated the genetic landscape associated with COVID-19 severity using whole-exome sequencing data from 325 Brazilian individuals recruited between 2020 and 2023. To prioritize variants related to disease severity, we applied a machine learning framework combining Support Vector Machine - Recursive Feature Elimination and SHAP interpretation. This approach encompasses 25
papers.summary: This study used whole-exome sequencing of 325 admixed Brazilian COVID-19 patients to identify host genetic factors associated with disease severity. The authors applied a machine learning framework (SVM-RFE with SHAP interpretation) to prioritize severity-associated variants and map them onto host genomic pathway landscapes. The work highlights the value of studying underrepresented admixed populations to uncover genetic contributors to COVID-19 outcomes.

papers.title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models.
papers.abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard-to-extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstr
papers.summary: The authors present a replicable, adaptable workflow that uses large language models to automatically extract species interaction data from ecological literature, addressing the challenge of synthesizing scattered information across hundreds of thousands of papers. The workflow is designed to be scalable and adaptable to a broad range of biological interaction types, with a demonstration of its application.

papers.title: MGP_HNSC32: A H&E Morphology-Derived 32-Gene Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and mult
papers.summary: The authors developed a transformer-based model (CTransPath) that predicts gene expression directly from H&E whole-slide images in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, then used the predicted expression to build a 32-gene prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) via Random Survival Forest. This links tumor morphology to a biologically interpretable gene-expression-based risk score, potentially enabling prognosis from routine histology slides without molecular assays.

papers.title: Cross hybridization inference for phylogenetic resolution-fluorescence in situ hybridization enables microbiome imaging with strain level taxonomic resolution.
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of microbial communities is a critical determinant of host-microbe interactions, yet species-level mapping remains challenging due to high 16S rRNA sequence homology and spectral crosstalk in multiplexed fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). To address this challenge, we developed Cross-hybridization Inference for Phylogenetic Resolution (CIPHR)-FISH, a pipeline that integrates strategic probe design with supervised machine learning. CIPHR-FISH transforms probe cross-hybridization, traditionally viewed as experimental noise, into informative molecular signatures.
papers.summary: The authors present CIPHR-FISH, a pipeline that combines strategic probe design with supervised machine learning to turn probe cross-hybridization—normally treated as noise—into informative signatures for distinguishing closely related microbes. This enables multiplexed FISH imaging of microbiomes at strain-level taxonomic resolution, addressing the challenge of high 16S rRNA homology and spectral crosstalk.

papers.title: Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses Identify NFKBIE as a Candidate Gene Associated with IS-II Neutrophil Differentiation in Lung Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: People undergoing lung transplantation may develop lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI), in which neutrophils contribute to the inflammatory response. However, the molecular features associated with distinct neutrophil states remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify candidate molecular features associated with the immunosuppressive-II (IS-II) neutrophil state, with particular attention to NFKBIE, an NF-κB inhibitor.
papers.summary: This study combined bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize neutrophil states in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI), a complication of lung transplantation. The authors identified NFKBIE, an inhibitor of NF-κB signaling, as a candidate gene associated with the immunosuppressive-II (IS-II) neutrophil differentiation state. The work nominates a specific molecular marker and potential regulatory node for a neutrophil subset implicated in post-transplant inflammation.

papers.title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanisms of Yinxieping Tablets in Psoriasis Treatment Based on Network Pharmacology, Bioinformatics, and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a prevalent immune-mediated chronic inflammatory skin disease, with a pathology defined by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and immune cell infiltration. Yinxieping Tablets (YXPT), a traditional Chinese medicine formula consisting solely of rosin, have been clinically used to alleviate psoriatic symptoms. However, their underlying mechanisms of action remain to be fully elucidated.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and bioinformatics to predict the molecular targets and pathways through which Yinxieping Tablets (a rosin-based traditional Chinese medicine) may treat psoriasis, then validates key predictions experimentally. The work aims to explain the clinical efficacy of YXPT at a mechanistic level, linking its components to psoriasis-related pathways such as keratinocyte proliferation and immune infiltration.

papers.title: Integrating proteomics to map immune landscape and protein biomarkers for risk stratification in childhood Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
papers.abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare pediatric disease with marked clinical heterogeneity. Current risk stratification relies on the extent of organ involvement and risk-organ status, yet reliable protein biomarkers for distinguishing LCH subtypes are lacking.
papers.summary: This study integrates proteomic profiling to characterize the immune landscape of childhood Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) and to identify protein biomarkers that could improve risk stratification beyond current organ-involvement-based criteria. The work aims to address the lack of reliable protein biomarkers for distinguishing LCH subtypes in this rare, clinically heterogeneous pediatric disease.

papers.title: Exploring biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms associated with 20 protein post-translational modifications in acute myocardial infarction based on transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a critical condition resulting from coronary occlusion, leading to myocardial necrosis and dysfunction. Protein posttranslational modifications (PTMs) regulate key inflammatory and signaling pathways in its pathogenesis. Accordingly, exploring transcriptomic signatures of genes encoding PTM-regulatory factors may provide valuable insights for improving early diagnosis and therapeutic stratification in AMI.
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptomic data to identify genes encoding regulators of 20 different protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) as potential biomarkers for acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The authors aim to link PTM-regulatory gene expression signatures to inflammatory and signaling pathways in AMI pathogenesis, with the goal of improving early diagnosis and therapeutic stratification. The work is exploratory, identifying candidate biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms rather than validating them experimentally.

papers.title: Identification and validation of biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson's disease based on GEO datasets.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by an unclear etiology and a lack of specific early diagnostic biomarkers. This study investigated novel biomarkers associated with mitochondrial dynamics (MD) dysfunction in PD.
papers.summary: This study analyzes public gene expression datasets (GEO) to identify biomarkers linked to mitochondrial dynamics dysfunction in Parkinson's disease. The authors identify candidate genes and validate them, aiming to improve early diagnosis of PD. The work is a bioinformatics reanalysis of existing data rather than a new experimental resource.

papers.title: Integrative analysis reveals shared biomarkers and pathways in osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis using machine learning and single-cell sequencing.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) are prevalent chronic diseases characterized by bone loss and immune dysregulation. Evidence suggests that patients with RA are at increased risk of developing OP; however, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic data with single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared biomarkers and molecular pathways between osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis, two conditions known to co-occur clinically. Using machine learning approaches, the authors pinpoint candidate genes and immune-related pathways common to both diseases, offering potential targets for diagnosis or therapy. The work is exploratory and relies on public datasets, so findings require experimental validation.

papers.title: Explainable computational framework for subtype classification and biomarker identification in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning.
papers.abstract: The precise classification of basal, classical, atypical, and mesenchymal subtypes of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is crucial for advancing precision oncology. Our research aims to develop an explainable subtype classification model for HNSCC.These molecular subtypes have been previously defined; reliable and meaningful computational methods for the classification of molecular subtypes and prioritization of molecular biomarkers for each subtype do not exist. We developed an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that classifies molecular subtypes based on combined tra
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable AI framework to classify HNSCC molecular subtypes (basal, classical, atypical, mesenchymal) and identify subtype-specific biomarkers, addressing the lack of reliable computational tools for this task. The model combines transcriptomic features with interpretability methods to prioritize biomarkers for each subtype, supporting precision oncology efforts in head and neck cancer.

papers.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.
papers.summary: This review surveys how AI and machine learning are being applied to BMP4 biology, spanning drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation. It highlights recent advances in predicting BMP4 structures at atomic resolution and using computational approaches to identify therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers for diseases like cancer, fibrosis, and FOP.

papers.title: Whole-genome sequencing-driven source tracing of foodborne diseases: from cgMLST/SNP typing toward an integrated framework of pan-genomics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Core-genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) and core-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (cgSNP) analysis have made whole-genome sequencing (WGS) the standard tool for foodborne disease surveillance. Fixed-threshold clustering is increasingly unreliable for highly clonal lineages such as Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 and Escherichia coli ST131, whose core genomes differ by only a handful of alleles even between unrelated strains. The central question is whether surveillance should keep simple, easy-to-interpret allele thresholds or move to probabilistic machine-learning models that also us
papers.summary: This review argues that fixed-threshold cgMLST and cgSNP clustering, the current standard for WGS-based foodborne disease source tracing, is unreliable for highly clonal lineages like Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 and E. coli ST131 where unrelated strains differ by only a few core-genome alleles. The authors propose moving toward an integrated framework combining pan-genomics and probabilistic machine-learning models to improve outbreak source attribution.

papers.title: Machine learning models integrating 2D and 3D intratumoral heterogeneity features from multi-sequence MRI: accurate prediction of perineural invasion in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) occurs in the majority of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and is strongly associated with local recurrence, neuropathic pain, and poor survival, yet no reliable method exists for its preoperative identification. Here, we developed and externally validated a multi-sequence MRI-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scoring framework integrated with machine learning for the non-invasive prediction of PNI in PDAC.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates a machine learning framework that uses 2D and 3D intratumoral heterogeneity features extracted from multi-sequence MRI to non-invasively predict perineural invasion in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The approach addresses a clinical gap, since PNI currently cannot be reliably identified before surgery despite its strong link to recurrence and poor survival.

papers.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
papers.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.
papers.summary: This study identifies shared molecular features between diabetes and colorectal cancer and tests whether the natural compound hupehenine can modulate these pathways in a diabetic-mimetic CRC model. Hupehenine suppressed tumor cell phenotypes and altered macrophage marker profiles, suggesting a potential therapeutic axis at the diabetes–CRC interface.

papers.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based model for predicting amputation risk in patients with lower extremity arterial disease and diabetes.
papers.abstract: Patients with lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) complicated by diabetes face substantial amputation risk. Pre-amputation death acts as a critical competing event that distorts risk estimation. Validated personalized prediction tools for this population remain scarce and hinder precise clinical interventions. This study aimed to develop and validate two complementary interpretable models for 12-month amputation risk in patients with LEAD and diabetes to support clinical decision-making.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated two interpretable machine learning models to predict 12-month amputation risk in patients with lower extremity arterial disease and diabetes, explicitly accounting for pre-amputation death as a competing event. The models aim to support personalized clinical decision-making in this high-risk population.

papers.title: A hybrid CNN-BiLSTM network with additive attention for automated four-stage classification of Alzheimer's disease from brain MRI.
papers.abstract: AD is a progressive and irreversible neurodegenerative disorder. Because the structural changes that accompany the earliest stages of the disease are subtle and easily overlooked, manual interpretation of MRI is time-consuming and prone to inter-observer disagreement. This study presents an end-to-end deep learning framework that fuses spatial and sequential reasoning to classify brain MRI into four clinically meaningful stages: Person with no dementia, Person with very mild dementia, Person with mild dementia, and Person with moderate dementia. An additive attention mechanism subsequently wei
papers.summary: This study develops a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and bidirectional LSTMs (BiLSTMs) for sequential reasoning, enhanced with an additive attention mechanism, to classify brain MRI scans into four stages of Alzheimer's disease severity. The approach aims to automate staging and reduce reliance on manual interpretation, which is time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. The abstract is truncated before results are reported, so the actual performance gains remain unclear.

papers.title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients.
papers.summary: This study develops a multimodal deep learning model that combines whole-slide pathology images with multiparametric MRI to predict, before surgery, which high-grade glioma patients will benefit from adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The model is designed to be interpretable and links its predictions to DNA damage repair pathways and immune characteristics. It aims to address the lack of reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification in this aggressive brain tumor.

papers.title: Systemic immune dysregulation and local barrier failure as predictors of septic shock in acute appendicitis: a large-scale multicenter interpretable machine learning study.
papers.abstract: The transition from localized acute appendicitis to systemic septic shock is driven by complex immune and metabolic dysregulation combined with anatomical barrier failure. Accurately predicting early hemodynamic deterioration remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable multimodal machine learning model by integrating systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic characteristics.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This multicenter study developed an interpretable multimodal machine learning model that combines systemic immunological profiles with local ultrasound features to predict progression from acute appendicitis to septic shock. The work aims to enable earlier identification of patients at risk of hemodynamic deterioration by capturing both immune dysregulation and anatomical barrier failure.

papers.title: Global thyroid cancer incidence in relation to dietary and socioeconomic factors: an ecological machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Thyroid cancer incidence has risen dramatically worldwide, with marked geographic heterogeneity suggesting dietary and environmental contributions beyond screening effects. The roles of specific dietary patterns in thyroid cancer remain poorly characterized at the global level.
papers.summary: This ecological study uses machine learning to examine how global thyroid cancer incidence correlates with dietary and socioeconomic factors across countries. It aims to identify which dietary patterns and socioeconomic indicators best explain the geographic heterogeneity in thyroid cancer rates, moving beyond screening-related explanations. The findings could highlight modifiable population-level factors, though the ecological design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Gradient boosting models for gallstone disease classification: A comparative study using demographic and clinical data.
papers.abstract: Gallstone disease is a prevalent gastrointestinal condition with a substantial healthcare burden. While abdominal ultrasonography is the established first-line diagnostic modality, opportunistic risk stratification using routinely collected health parameters remains underexplored. This study evaluated the discriminatory capacity of four gradient boosting machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and HistGBM) for classifying gallstone status using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory features. A retrospective clinical dataset of 319 patients (161 gallstone-positive
papers.summary: This study compared four gradient boosting machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, HistGBM) for classifying gallstone disease using demographic, bioimpedance, and routine laboratory data from 319 patients. The work explores whether routinely collected health parameters can support opportunistic risk stratification as a complement to ultrasound-based diagnosis.

papers.title: Routine Metabolic Laboratory Profile and Time-Stratified Machine-Learning Risk Stratification of Rosacea: A Combined Retrospective-Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Rosacea has been linked with systemic metabolic abnormalities in case-control studies, but most such evidence compares rosacea patients with healthy controls rather than asking which patients within a rosacea population carry the greatest metabolic burden. We aimed to describe the metabolic profile of a real-world rosacea outpatient cohort and build a time-stratified, outcome-independent machine-learning model ranking which routine metabolic indicators predict metabolic syndrome status.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the metabolic profiles of a real-world rosacea outpatient cohort and develops a time-stratified machine-learning model to rank routine metabolic indicators by their ability to predict metabolic syndrome status within rosacea patients. Rather than comparing rosacea patients to healthy controls, it focuses on stratifying metabolic risk among rosacea patients themselves.

papers.title: The potential role of large language models in addressing phenoconversion in pharmacogenomics.
papers.abstract: Pharmacogenomics (PGx) is a cornerstone of precision medicine, enabling individualized drug therapy by identifying genetic factors that influence drug disposition and response. However, genotype-based predictions frequently fail to reflect actual drug-metabolizing capacity because enzyme activity can be modified by non-genetic factors, including concomitant medications, inflammation, organ dysfunction, aging, smoking, pregnancy, and other environmental influences. Phenoconversion can generate substantial discrepancies between genotype-predicted and observed metabolic phenotypes, contributing t
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses phenoconversion in pharmacogenomics—the phenomenon where a patient's actual drug-metabolizing enzyme activity diverges from what their genotype predicts, due to factors like drug interactions, inflammation, organ dysfunction, aging, smoking, and pregnancy. The authors propose that large language models could help integrate these diverse non-genetic factors to improve phenotype prediction and guide more accurate individualized drug therapy.

papers.title: Bridging large language model-based agents and workflow languages for automated multi-perspective analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data.
papers.abstract: In single-cell RNA sequencing data analysis, the same dataset can be examined from multiple complementary perspectives, each requiring different analytical strategies and potentially leading to distinct biological interpretations. Systematically exploring such diverse strategies in a reproducible and scalable manner remains challenging.
papers.summary: This paper connects LLM-based agents with workflow languages to automate multi-perspective analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data. The approach lets the same dataset be explored through several complementary analytical strategies in a reproducible and scalable way, rather than relying on a single fixed pipeline. This addresses a key bottleneck in scRNA-seq interpretation, where different analytical choices can yield distinct biological conclusions.

papers.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-ECForest, a two-stage machine learning pipeline that combines protein language model embeddings from ESM-2 with random forest classifiers to predict Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. The hierarchical two-stage design addresses class imbalance and the hierarchical organization of enzyme functions, aiming to improve robustness over sequence-similarity-based annotation. This offers a practical approach for scaling enzyme functional annotation to growing sequence databases.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a widely used non-invasive neurophysiological technique for analyzing brain dynamics and diagnosing neurological diseases. However, the non-stationary nature, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability of EEG signals cause significant challenges to traditional analytical approaches. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful computational tool for EEG analysis, which enables automated feature learning and improved diagnostic accuracy with minimal human-driven feature extraction. This review systematically explains computational approa
papers.summary: This systematic review surveys deep learning methods for analyzing EEG signals to diagnose neurological diseases. It covers computational approaches that automatically learn features from noisy, variable EEG data, addressing challenges that traditional methods struggle with. The review aims to consolidate how these techniques improve diagnostic accuracy with less manual feature engineering.
